lead: Model integrity and agent evaluation are the decisions to revisit today. Microsoft describes a no-retraining backdoor that can survive standard evaluations, making verified weight provenance and restricted tool authority part of model intake rather than optional red-team extras. AWS’s evaluation guidance complements that threat by tying tests to business outcomes and observable behaviours, while its invocation data-lake example shows how to attribute usage across accounts. For long-running agents, Thoughtworks’ durable-execution pattern is a useful design review: replay and recovery must account for external effects, not just restore process state.

items.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
items.summary: Microsoft researchers describe a no-retraining technique that can reprogramme fewer than 10 dormant neurons to trigger malicious agent commands while the model passes standard evaluations. The post says weight provenance and comparison with original weights are important detection controls; the attack is research, and the post does not state a product release, regional scope or pricing.
items.so_what: Tighten model-intake checks for weight provenance and integrity, and keep tool and terminal permissions bounded because behavioural evaluation alone may miss a triggered backdoor.

items.title: The agent evaluation playbook: Built-in, DeepEval, and AutoEval on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Evaluations
items.summary: AWS demonstrates combining built-in, DeepEval and AutoEval evaluators in AgentCore Evaluations, mapping each agent behaviour to an evaluation at trace or session level. Its examples start from business outcomes such as task completion, grounded research and moderation quality; regional availability and pricing are not stated.
items.so_what: Trial the outcome-to-behaviour mapping in your evaluation harness, including privacy leakage and skipped steps alongside completion, and compare evaluator results with labelled cases before using them as release gates.

items.title: v1.109.0
items.summary: LiteLLM v1.109.0 states that its Docker images are signed with cosign and documents verification using a public key pinned to an immutable commit. This changes the software-supply-chain check for deployments using these images; service regions and pricing are not applicable to the release notes.
items.so_what: Adopt signature verification in your image-promotion pipeline, pinning the published key by commit hash and testing verification in CI before rollout.

items.title: How TCS built an agentic test orchestrator with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.summary: AWS describes TCS’s agentic test orchestrator, which turns requirements into governed executable tests using specialised agents and per-tenant isolation. The candidate reports an 88% reduction in testing effort in an internal benchmark; independent replication, pricing and regional scope are not stated.
items.so_what: Use the architecture as a pilot reference, but require a defined effort baseline, test-quality measures and tenant-isolation checks before relying on the reported reduction in your own business case.

items.title: Release v2.67.0 (2026-11-10)
items.summary: Pydantic AI v2.67.0 adds support for dynamic subagents under durable execution and changes ArtifactScanner matching to strip default-ignorable characters and flag hidden variation selectors. The release also changes RepoContext instruction-file loading by default, so migration compatibility needs review; service regions and pricing are not stated.
items.so_what: Trial the scanner and durable-subagent changes against your artifact and recovery threat cases, and review the new instruction-file discovery behaviour before upgrading production agents.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock tokenomics data lake
items.summary: AWS provides a CloudFormation, Lambda and SQL example that consolidates Bedrock invocation logs from linked accounts into a central Athena-queryable table. The design supports review of prompts, responses, token counts, model choice and per-invocation cost; regional scope and service pricing are not stated in the post.
items.so_what: Benchmark the central attribution pattern against your current cost and audit telemetry, with explicit access controls for prompt and response data before exposing cross-team views.

items.title: Start and Restore GPU Workloads in Seconds with NVIDIA Snapshot
items.summary: NVIDIA describes Snapshot, an open-source Kubernetes checkpoint-and-restore system that captures initialised CPU and GPU memory for inference workloads. Its tests report restore times of 3.6–42.7 seconds and 8–36× speedups over cold starts across tested configurations, but exclude infrastructure provisioning and image loading; the post gives no pricing or general regional availability.
items.so_what: Trial it against your inference autoscaling and recovery path, reproducing restore measurements on compatible hardware and including provisioning, image loading and failure recovery in the comparison.

items.title: Long-horizon agents and durable execution
items.summary: Thoughtworks’ Kiran Prakash explains durable execution for agents that run over days or weeks: record each external step so a restarted workflow can skip completed work and rebuild state. The article distinguishes recovery from correctness and discusses retries, human and system waits, and unseen external outcomes; it is an architectural explanation, not a measured benchmark, and gives no pricing or regional scope.
items.so_what: Use the durable-execution model in a workflow design review, testing idempotency, reconciliation and ambiguous external effects rather than treating replay as proof that an action happened only once.

items.title: Batch Intelligence at Scale: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent LLM Workflows with Built-In Resilience
items.summary: InfoQ’s presentation summary describes Walmart Global Tech’s nightly multi-agent inventory-forecasting workflows across 4,700 stores, addressing schema violations, data mismatches and network drops with MCP grounding and loop agents. It reports cloud inference costs falling from more than USD 100,000 to USD 10,000 per month after moving from PTUs to pay-as-you-go; these are presenter-reported figures, and the page does not give an independent cost analysis or regional scope.
items.so_what: Benchmark the batch, resilience and inference-pricing pattern against your own workload, verifying equivalent throughput and service levels before treating the reported monthly spend change as transferable.

items.title: LLM Reliability Layers Under Test: Accuracy, Yield, and the Limits of Verification
items.summary: The article reports a comparison of reliability layers and argues that voting and self-correction may withhold uncertain outputs without correcting the underlying errors. It recommends measuring yield as well as accuracy and replacing generation with deterministic lookups where possible; the reported evaluation is author-led, not independently replicated, and the accessible account does not establish a universal result.
items.so_what: Use the accuracy-versus-yield distinction in your evaluation design, and benchmark deterministic retrieval against stacked verification on your own labelled cases before adding more checks.

items.title: @arizeai/phoenix-client@8.0.0
items.summary: Phoenix client v8.0.0 moves its OpenTelemetry integration to OpenTelemetry JS 3 and changes the type returned by register(), as well as the required source and options for custom span processors. This is a major compatibility change for tracing integrations; regions and pricing are not applicable to the release notes.
items.so_what: Trial the upgrade in a tracing compatibility branch and validate span emission and custom processors before adopting it across instrumented services.

items.title: DSPy 3.5: A Lighter, Faster Foundation
items.summary: DSPy 3.5 graduates RLM, Flex and GEPA from experimental status and introduces a lighter LM layer with new History and image capabilities for RLM. The release changes prompts, defaults and APIs from 3.4.1 and calls for re-evaluation of optimised programs; pricing and regional scope are not stated.
items.so_what: Trial the graduated modules on a non-production branch and rerun your prompt/program evaluations before upgrading, since changed defaults can shift behaviour even when application code still runs.
